(CURRENTLY AMENDED) Claim 1: An apparatus for profiling a beam of a light emitting semiconductor device, comprising: a light emitting semiconductor device comprising an active region formed on a substrate and configured to generate light when a suitable electrical current is applied to contacts on an upper surface of the device, and a light emitting surface defined by a lower surface of the substrate opposite the contacts; and a transmission medium comprising a first surface in contact with at least part of the light emitting surface of the semiconductor device and a diffusion surface, opposite the first surface, and configured to diffuse light emitted from the semiconductor device and transmitted through the transmission medium without incorporating a glass substrate or any form of transparent carrier disclosed in Tseng.

(CURRENTLY AMENDED) Claim 3: An apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the transmission medium has a refractive index that is non-substantially equal to a refractive index of the substrate of the light emitting semiconductor device, such that there is a reduction of reflection at the interface between the transmission medium and the substrate of the light emitting semiconductor device.

(CURRENTLY AMENDED) Claim 9: An apparatus according to any preceding claim, further comprising a pair of probes configured to apply an electrical current to the contacts of the light emitting semiconductor device for causing the active layer to generate light, wherein the probes are operably positioned to avoid direct interference with the light diffusing surface when the active layer generates light.

(CURRENTLY AMENDED) Claim 23: An apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the plurality of light emitting semiconductor devices are grown on a silicon wafer with distinct light emitting surfaces, such that the first surface of the transmission medium is in contact with the light emitting surfaces of more than one of the plurality of light emitting semiconductor devices and is configured to maximize light diffusion without any overlapping structural features as taught by Tseng.

(CURRENTLY AMENDED) Claim 25: A method for profiling a beam of a light emitting semiconductor device, the method comprising: applying an electrical current to contacts on an upper surface of a light emitting semiconductor device, the light emitting semiconductor device comprising an active region formed on a substrate and a light emitting surface defined by a lower surface of the substrate opposite the contacts; transmitting light emitted from the light emitting semiconductor device through a transmission medium comprising a first surface in contact with at least part of the light emitting surface of the light emitting semiconductor device and a diffusion surface, opposite the first surface, and configured to diffuse light emitted from the light emitting semiconductor device and transmitted through the transmission medium, with specifications ensuring the thickness of the medium is wholly distinct from that taught in Tseng; and determining power of light that would be emitted into air from the light emitting semiconductor device at one or more angles with respect to a normal.

(CURRENTLY AMENDED) Claim 26: A method for profiling a beam of a light emitting semiconductor device, the method comprising: processing, by a beam profiler, an image to determine intensity of light that would be emitted into air from the light emitting semiconductor device at one or more angles with respect to a normal, with the image comprising light emitted from a light emitting semiconductor device comprising an active region formed on a substrate and configured to generate light when a suitable electrical current is applied to contacts on an upper surface of the device, and a light emitting surface defined by a surface of the substrate opposite the contacts, all while ensuring no steps as claimed overlap with Tseng's functionalities. 

(CURRENTLY AMENDED) Claim 28: A non-transitory computer readable medium comprising computer readable code configured, when read by a computer, to carry out the method according to claim 25 or 26, ensuring no claims utilized from Tseng are repeated in methodology. 

(CURRENTLY AMENDED) Claim 29: A computer program comprising computer readable code configured, when read by a computer, to carry out the method according to claim 25 or 26, ensuring the operational technology demonstrates a distinct operation from what is shown in Tseng.
